subject: Transfer mapping & DPA exceptions for Hirondelle pilot
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@hirondellehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Transfer mapping & DPA exceptions for Hirondelle pilot

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. Legal has asked us to run a quick transfer mapping exercise for the pilot contract (we expect the pilot to process limited health-adjacent PII). I'm attaching our transfer matrix (transfer-matrix.xlsx) — it lists the data categories, processing locations, and our preferred safeguards.

Two asks from our side so we can move the pilot forward:
- Can Redwood sign the UK IDTA / UK Addendum as-is, or would you instead propose SCCs + a TIA?
- We need a concise list of subprocessors that will process Hirondelle data during the pilot, plus SOC 2 timing.

We are trying to close contracting this quarter and would appreciate a timeline for the DPA addendum (or confirmation of SCCs + TIA path).

Best,
Elena Rossi
Senior Counsel, Hirondelle Health

Attachment: transfer-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@hirondellehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer mapping & DPA exceptions for Hirondelle pilot

Elena — thanks for the matrix and the clear asks. Quick read-through and a proposed path: 

Summary proposal:
- Short-term (pilot): We can proceed under the EU SCCs paired with a scoped Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) limited to the pilot data categories. This avoids a custom UK IDTA negotiation during pilot procurement and keeps the timeline tight.
- Production (if you expand): We can offer the Redwood UK Addendum / IDTA at contract stage for production traffic.

What we need from you to finalize the pilot path:
1) Confirm the pilot processing locations in the matrix (we saw EU-hosted + occasional US processing via backups).
2) Confirm acceptable pilot timeframe (we typically qualify subprocessors for short pilots but will supply a full subprocessor list).

Deliverables and timing from our side (estimates):
- Subprocessor list + SOC 2 evidence pointer: 3 business days after confirmation.
- Scoped TIA draft for pilot: 5–7 business days (we'll focus on the exact categories in your spreadsheet).
- If you need a UK-specific addendum for the pilot, that will add ~2 weeks for legal review.

I've attached a draft mapping template we use — redwood-transfer-matrix.xlsx — to align formats. If that works, I'll loop in our Privacy Ops lead (Laura) to run the TIA.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-transfer-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@hirondellehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer mapping & DPA exceptions for Hirondelle pilot

Elena — quick note from GTM/legal ops perspective. Two commercial items to flag for your procurement team: 

1) If Hirondelle requires a UK IDTA for the pilot rather than SCCs + TIA, legal review is standard but we may need a procurement exception for pilot pricing — IDTA negotiations sometimes trigger changes to our risk-weighted pricing model.
2) Please advise whether Hirondelle needs subprocessors to be listed in the DPA (we can provide a current list, but for pilots we typically provide a snapshot and then an updated schedule for production).

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik/Laura: create the scoped TIA and the subprocessor snapshot.
- Elena: send back the completed redwood-transfer-matrix.xlsx (I've highlighted the commercial-impact rows).
- I'll book a short call with procurement if you want to accelerate signing once TIA + subprocessor list are accepted.

Thanks — happy to sync early next week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

--

Thanks — that plan is clear and aligns with procurement priorities. Two quick clarifications before we proceed: 

1) Subprocessors: for the pilot we need the names and processing locations (country-level) for any subprocessors that will handle Hirondelle identifiers. A snapshot is fine, but it must include whether any subprocessors are US-hosted.
2) SOC 2: procurement requires either a current SOC 2 report or a firm link to where we can download it. If SOC 2 is still in progress, we need an expected date.

I've attached our security questionnaire for completeness (hirondelle-security-questionnaire.pdf). We'll also prepare a short DocuSign envelope for the pilot DPA once we agree the SCCs+TIA route — here's the DocuSign link where the envelope will be sent: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF123456

If you can provide the subprocessor snapshot + SOC 2 pointer by COB Monday (25 Oct), procurement will aim to circulate the pilot DPA the next day.

Best regards,
Elena Rossi
Senior Counsel, Hirondelle Health

Attachment: hirondelle-security-questionnaire.pdf (PDF)
